newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia launches effort to promote Batam airport.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia launches effort to promote Batam airport.

text.p: Indonesia said on Tuesday it has launched efforts to develop Batam, an island near Singapore, into a cargo hub for the country with a request to German flag carrier Lufthansa to run services to the island.

Research and Technology Minister Jusuf Habibie, who also heads the Batam Island Industrial Development Authority, said in a written report to parliament that Lufthansa Air Cargo had been asked to service Batam's Hang Nadim Airport.

"As part of the efforts to have the benefit of Hang Nadim airport as an international cargo airport we have already sounded out Lufthansa Air Cargo to pioneer flights from Batam to Europe," Habibie said.
"It is hoped the flights will become a reality in the near future and reduce costs of exporting Batam's products because up until now all exports from Batam go through Singapore," he said.

The report said international flights from Hang Nadim start in November when Garuda Indonesia begins a weekly DC-10 flight between Batam and Jeddah in Saudi Arabia before upgrading this to three flights in March.
The same month Garuda will start twice weekly B747-400 flights to London via Batam from Jakarta and Airbus A300 or A330 flights to Manila via Batam, the report said.
Flights to Taipei and Beijing via Hang Nadim, upgraded in December 1995, are also under consideration, it said.

Earlier this month, Indonesian Transport Minister Haryanto Dhanutirto was quoted as saying the government wanted all foreign air cargo planes servicing Indonesia to stop at Batam. Domestic carriers would then ferry cargo within the country, it has said.
The government wants to develop Batam as an air cargo hub to rival Singapore's Changi airport, about 20 km to the northwest.
